items.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023
items.q: where the waiter opened up this jazz club in Aspen. He said, “Hey man can you come?” “Bill? Really, is that you?”

ctx.x: That’s neat. That’s a fraternity of musicians. And I think it behooves people to know that to act professional in whatever thing you are doing because as you say, twenty years down the line some someone’s going to think —

Yes. That’s a great point. And you know if you’re playing in a jazz club and you’re cool with the staff, you know you go out of your way, “Hey man, thanks for taking care of us.” You know that dude could start running a jazz club. And that’s happened to me before, where the waiter opened up this jazz club in Aspen. He said, “Hey man can you come?” “Bill? Really, is that you?” So just what you’re saying. You know be aware of your environment, who you’re working for and just make sure you’re present. Because you…

What was the other, after Dry Jack the — I have to insert one thing because this stuck in my head, for our viewers, I was teaching at the school they you had sort of recently graduated from, at Vernon, Verona, Sherrill and you guys were together pre Inner City and you asked me to come over to this house where you were all living I think cause you wanted to learn some, I don’t know what it was, theory.
